from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Point:
    x: int
    y: int = 0


p = Point(3)
print(p, p.x, p == Point(3, 0))

steps.description: Point declares x and y as fields. You give y a default of zero, while x remains a required constructor argument.
Point(3) supplies x and uses the default y. You store that object in p.

steps.answer: Yes. Both Point objects have x equal to 3 and y equal to 0.
steps.question: Will p compare equal to Point(3, 0)?
